claim: FEMM fieldplot pack: OC peak |B| 2.25 T, loaded Path B −30° peak 2.69 T, 4096 probes; Tony 2D maps + 3D |B| landscapes + plotly HTML; ship_ok false

claims.why: fieldplot_pack_manifest.json cases.oc_full.bmag_peak_t = 2.2496272626858067 ≈ 2.25 T. The OC solve script (em_fia_fieldplot_pack.py _run_field_sample) computes np.nanmax(bmag_t) and the manifest prints that as the peak. Grid 64x64 = 4096 probes is also consistent (grid.full_n=64, full_probes=4096). The 2.25 T value is exactly what the manifest reports.

fieldplot_pack_manifest.json cases.loaded_path_b_full.bmag_peak_t = 2.6899865014133693 ≈ 2.69 T. The operating_point.current_angle_electrical_deg = -30.0 and kind = loaded_path_b_kit_case_op confirm the −30° electrical Path B kit-case point. 4096 probes also matches.

Manifest grid.full_probes = 4096 and full_n = 64 → 64*64 = 4096. All three sampled cases (oc_full, loaded_path_b_full, loaded_path_b_pole_zoom) show n_probes of 4096, 4096, and 3136 respectively. The '4096 probes' figure matches the two full-machine maps referenced in the claim.

em_fia_fieldplot_pack.py defines plot_tony_2d and the run_pack() _emit() block writes <stem>_tony_bmag.png for both OC and loaded cases. Manifest artefacts list includes 01-oc-full_tony_bmag.png and 02-loaded-full_tony_bmag.png, both present as new binary files in the diff.

plot_surface_3d() in the script produces <stem>_surface3d.png (and write_plotly_html() produces the interactive HTML). Manifest artefacts include 01-oc-full_surface3d.png, 02-loaded-full_surface3d.png, 03-loaded-pole-zoom_surface3d.png, and 04-loaded-airgap-ring3d.png — all present as new binary files. These are 3D landscape renderings of |B|(x,y) (height encodes flux density).

write_plotly_html() in the script calls go.Figure(go.Surface(...)).write_html(..., include_plotlyjs='cdn'), generating 01-oc-full_interactive3d.html and 02-loaded-full_interactive3d.html — both present in the diff with valid Plotly.newPlot(...) content embedded, using plotly-3.7.0.min.js from cdn.plot.ly. Manifest interactive_html list matches.

fieldplot_pack_manifest.json ship_ok = false is explicit at the top level, and the script's release_statement and honesty.not_claimed list reinforce 'ship_ok / homologation' as not claimed. Cover PNG text and docstring also state ship_ok false.

review.weakest_link: All claims are directly anchored in the new manifest.json and the artefacts the script emits; none require inference beyond what the diff shows. The closest thing to a weak link is '3D |B| landscapes' (the script is honest that these are 2D FEMM |B|(x,y) extruded as a landscape, not a 3D FE solve) — but the claim phrasing '3D |B| landscapes' matches the file naming (_surface3d.png, interactive3d.html) so it is supported as labelled.
review.one_line_summary: Every claim in the commit message is directly supported by the new fieldplot_pack_manifest.json and the artefacts (Tony maps, 3D landscapes, plotly HTML, 4096-probe grids, OC 2.25 T / loaded −30° 2.69 T peaks, ship_ok=false) emitted by em_fia_fieldplot_pack.py.

missed.issue: The reported loaded full-map “peak 2.69 T” is not the pack's actual loaded peak: the pole-zoom case in the same manifest reaches 3.0399 T. The result is resolution/window dependent, yet the cover/claim presents 2.69 T as a peak.
missed.why_it_matters: This understates the highest sampled flux density by about 13% and can hide steel saturation risk. A coarse Cartesian grid cannot support an unqualified peak claim, especially when the finer follow-up sample already disproves it.
missed.how_to_test: Load both NPZ files and compare np.nanmax(bmag_t); assert that the headline peak is the maximum across every generated case, or label it explicitly as “64x64 full-map sampled peak.” Add a grid-convergence run (64/128/256 or adaptive refinement around high-B cells) and require convergence before publishing a peak.

missed.issue: The A_z fallback is effectively broken for this full Cartesian grid. Since only about the circular machine interior has valid FEMM values, the `> 0.9` finite-A threshold selects the fallback. `_inject_probes` inserts NaNs outside the mesh, and `-np.cumsum(by, axis=1)` propagates the first outside-mesh NaN through each row, leaving `a_reconstructed` NaN across nearly all/all rows.
missed.why_it_matters: The Tony plots claim flux-line contours, but their contour source can be entirely invalid. This silently changes the output from “|B| map plus flux lines” to only a magnitude map; no test detects it.
missed.how_to_test: Run the pack and assert `np.isfinite(sample.a_reconstructed).any()` and that a meaningful fraction of in-machine points is finite. Inspect the contour artist/PNG for nonzero contour paths. Prefer using FEMM-returned A directly with a geometry mask, or reconstruct only over contiguous valid segments with NaN-aware integration.

missed.issue: The interactive HTML is not self-contained: it requires Plotly from `https://cdn.plot.ly`. Opening an artifact offline, behind a corporate CSP, or after CDN/integrity/version changes leaves no plot.
missed.why_it_matters: A checked-in evidence pack is expected to remain reviewable. The generated HTML silently fails for air-gapped CI/review environments despite being presented as a shipped interactive artifact.
missed.how_to_test: Open both HTML files with network disabled and assert a Plotly graph is rendered. Generate self-contained HTML (`include_plotlyjs=True`) or package a pinned local Plotly asset and test it from a file URL.

generality_concerns: The generator is presented as a fieldplot pack but is tightly coupled to the FE-front Path-B deck, 48-slot/eight-pole phase-belt assumptions, `rotor.hole[0].magnet_0`, and a fixed -30 electrical-degree operating point. It is not a reusable field-plot pipeline for arbitrary motor archetypes without extracting deck/phase-map/material access behind an explicit adapter.

The “one pole-pair zoom” is not general or accurately named: `_pole_pair_window` derives `2π / rotor_poles`, which is one mechanical pole span, then uses an axis-aligned heuristic near +X. It will not reliably contain a pole pair or corresponding tooth geometry for other pole counts/rotor orientations.

The 3D landscapes and air-gap ring are display transformations of sparse 2D samples. The code labels this honestly in the manifest, but a generic consumer can still compare their visual height/colour scales across OC and loaded plots even though each plot auto-normalizes independently.
review.one_line_summary: Block: the headline loaded peak is contradicted by the included zoom result, and the advertised flux contours can be invalidated by NaN propagation.
Claim matches the pack: OC/loaded peaks ~2.25/2.69 T on 64²=4096 probes, Tony/3D/plotly artefacts present, ship_ok false.
